title: Sunny and the Big Wind
description: A big wind sweeps through the bush, and Little Sonny the quokka learns to feel it, not fear it. A brave, breezy bedtime story for little ones. Part of Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
One afternoon, the wind came.

Not a gentle breeze. Not a soft sigh through the leaves. A real wind. A big, rushing, swirling wind that bent the grasses sideways and sent the eucalyptus leaves spinning into the sky.

Sunny sat very still at first, his ears flattened, his eyes wide.

The wind roared through the treetops. The branches swayed and creaked. A shower of bark fell softly to the ground near his feet.

Sunny blinked.

And then — slowly — something changed.

He took a deep breath. The air rushing into him was cool and full of the smell of rain somewhere far away. It was alive. The whole world felt suddenly, completely, vigorously alive.

He stood up and spread his little arms out wide.

The wind pushed against him. It ruffled his fur all the wrong way. It made his ears flutter.

He couldn't help it. He laughed.

Not a big laugh. Just a small, surprised, delighted laugh.

The leaves swirled all around him like a slow golden storm. The tall grasses danced. The whole bush seemed to shiver and sing.

Sunny stood in the middle of it all, arms out, eyes closed, feeling the wind move all around him and through him.

And slowly, slowly, the wind began to quieten.

It softened to a breeze. The leaves settled. The grasses stilled.

The bush breathed out.

Sunny lowered his arms and looked around. Everything was the same as before. But also, somehow, cleaned. Cleared. Fresh.

He found a sheltered spot beneath a low wattle bush and curled up in the soft leaf litter.

Above him, the last of the wind moved through the high branches like a long, slow sigh.

Goodnight, little Sunny. Goodnight, big wind. Goodnight, brave and breezy day.
